summary: Ferry County, WA platform lookout built around 1930 on the Colville NF; FFLOS index lists it as gone; the register notes fire-ring rocks still in place.

facts.design: Platform about 30 ft tall, built from three trimmed trees, reached by ladder; rag camp near the base
facts.status_note: FFLOS Washington index lists the platform as Gone; the register detail page calls it a lookout site and describes remains (fire-ring rocks) without giving a date

events.note: Register Built field reads 'circa 1930'; year is approximate
Registered April 3, 2018 as US 1712, WA 442; nominated by Rod Fosback

evidence.supports: design: platform about 30 ft tall from three trimmed trees, reached by ladder
evidence.quote: The lookout was a platform tower 30 feet tall using 3 trees cut and trimmed to that height and accessed using a ladder.

evidence.supports: rag camp stood near the base
evidence.quote: A rag camp was near its base with the large rocks used to block wind from the fire ring still in place.

evidence.supports: local recognition as separate from Skalawag Ridge, with records
evidence.quote: Locals recognize this lookout as separate from Skalawag Ridge Lookout and there are supporting records.

evidence.supports: register suggests it may have been the patrol lookout used with Skalawag Ridge
evidence.quote: It may be, however, the patrol lookout used in conjunction with Skalawag Ridge Lookout.

evidence.supports: registered April 3, 2018, nominated by Rod Fosback
administered by the U.S. Forest Service
index lists the platform as gone
evidence.quote: Paradise Peak Ferry 48.60056 -118.41833 Platform Gone FFLOS US 1712, WA 442

sources.title: Paradise Peak Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites (Forest Fire Lookout Association)

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' rests on the FFLOS index line; the detail page never states a fate in so many words. Brief's 1930 is 'circa 1930' on the register. Possible link to Skalawag Ridge is unresolved: willhiteweb.com's Skalawag page (https://www.willhiteweb.com/washington_fire_lookouts/skalawag_ridge/lookout_097.htm, not cited in the story) says a pole platform about two miles northwest of Skalawag Ridge was 'apparently still there in the 1980s'; that page does not name Paradise Peak, so the two may or may not be the same structure. No staffing, fire or access information found in the sources read. Access left out of facts.
